proofs.proof_tex:
Because \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
 0<\eta_\alpha=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}<1-2\alpha.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), applied with \(\eta=\eta_\alpha\), therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge
 \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha).
\]
This invocation uses Definition \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\), so its infimum is over all of the stated schedule-independent Markov kernels and its coverage and length probabilities are computed under the same extended law.

For the upper inequality, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}upper\text{-}frontier}\) constructs one schedule-independent kernel \(K^\star\in\mathcal C_\alpha\) and proves
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}
 \mathbb E^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}
 [\operatorname{len}(I^\star)]
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(K\in\mathcal C_\alpha\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\) yields
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}
 \mathbb E^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}
 [\operatorname{len}(I^\star)]
 \le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
This proves the universal bracket.

For the computable supplement, let \(\mathcal S_W\) be the finite collection of all subsets of \(\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}\) satisfying the probability constraint displayed in the theorem.  The empty set belongs to \(\mathcal S_W\), because its masked event is the whole record space and hence has probability one.  For every \(S\in\mathcal S_W\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:masked\text{-}focal\text{-}modulus\text{-}certificate}\), with \(\gamma=\Gamma\), gives
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \ge 2M\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b}.
\]
The set \(\mathcal S_W\) is finite, so taking its maximum preserves the inequality.  Multiplication by \(\eta_\alpha>0\) and the already proved modulus lower bound give
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \ge
 \eta_\alpha
 \max_{S\in\mathcal S_W}
 \left\{2M\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b}\right\}.
\]
The final assertion of the masked-focal lemma writes each probability constraint as a finite sum of products of known predictable propensities on zero-outcome histories, proving the claimed computability.

It remains to prove that the absent lower comparison with \(\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\) is false, rather than merely unavailable from these arguments.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}alpha\text{-}only\text{-}obstruction}\) constructs, for the fixed \(\alpha\) and \(M\), admissible experiments indexed by \(n\) for which
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
If a constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) obeyed \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) for every experiment satisfying the primitive conditions, then applying it to every member of this sequence and dividing by \(2M>0\) would give
\[
 0<c_\alpha
 \le
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}
 \quad\text{for every sufficiently large }n.
\]
Taking \(n\to\infty\) contradicts \(c_\alpha>0\).  Thus no such alpha-only constant exists on the primitive adaptive class.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and \(M>0\).  There is a sequence of admissible three-block adaptive platform experiments \(\mathcal D_n\), each having \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(\Gamma=0\), and a strictly positive propensity floor \(p_{\min,n}\), such that
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, over the primitive adaptive-design class there is no constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) for which \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) holds uniformly.  The obstruction is a low-propensity history whose probability is below the permitted miscoverage level, not a failure of positivity in any member of the sequence.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac{\alpha}{2},
 \qquad
 \delta_n=\frac{\varepsilon}{n}.
\]
For every sufficiently large integer \(n\), take \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(q_2=1\), and \((n_1,n_2,n_3)=(1,n,1)\).  Take the platform-arm set \(\mathcal Z_n=\{z_0,z_1,a\}\), where \(a\notin\{z_0,z_1\}\), and set
\[
 A_1=\{z_0,a\},\qquad
 A_2=\{z_0,z_1\},\qquad
 A_3=\{z_0\}.
\]
At the only position in block \(1\), assign \(a\) with probability \(\varepsilon\) and \(z_0\) with probability \(1-\varepsilon\), and define
\[
 E=\{Z_{11}=a\}.
\]
Thus \(E\) is known before block \(2\), and \(P^O_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(E)=\varepsilon\) for every fixed schedule \(Y\).  At every position in block \(2\), set
\[
 p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta_n,&E,\\
  1/2,&E^c,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 p_{2i}(z_0\mid H_{2i})=1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i}),
\]
and assign \(z_0\) with probability one in block \(3\); every arm outside the displayed availability set receives probability zero.  These probabilities are measurable with respect to the pre-assignment histories, so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) holds by construction.  Their support is exactly the displayed availability set, and \(z_1\) is available exactly in \(W\), establishing Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:availability\text{-}support}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:availability\text{-}window}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 0<\delta_n\le
 \min\{\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon,1/2,1-\delta_n,1\},
\]
so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:propensity\text{-}floor}\) holds with \(p_{\min,n}=\delta_n>0\).  We use the class \(\mathcal Y_{M,0}\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def:schedule\text{-}family}\): Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:control\text{-}tv}\) require bounded fixed potential outcomes and equal control block means, respectively.  Hence each constructed experiment is in the primitive class.

We first evaluate its frozen optimized radius.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:concurrent\text{-}weights}\) gives \(u_2=1\) and \(u_1=u_3=0\).  The focal-arm summand in Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}design\text{-}scale}\) is schedule independent because its propensity is a function only of \(E\).  All other summands in \(\mathsf G_{\mathcal D_n}\) are nonnegative.  Therefore, for every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal B)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)
 &\ge
 8M^2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{n^2}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 \left[
  \frac{1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}
       {p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}
 \right]\\
 &=\frac{8M^2}{n}
 \left\{
  \varepsilon\frac{1-\delta_n}{\delta_n}
  +(1-\varepsilon)\frac{1-1/2}{1/2}
 \right\}\\
 &=8M^2\left\{1+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{n}\right\}
 \ge 8M^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The expectation is the same for every \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\), so it remains a valid lower bound after the schedule supremum defining \(\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}\).  The middle equality is also the rare-branch assignment-law averaging identity in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:rare\text{-}history\text{-}stress\text{-}test}\).  Since \(\mathsf B_0(v)\ge0\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}frontier}\) and \(\alpha<1/2\) imply
\[
 \Psi_{\alpha,0}(v)
 \ge \sqrt{\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)/\alpha}
 \ge M\sqrt{8/\alpha}>2M.
\]
This holds for every feasible \(v\), and clipping in that definition therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M.
\]

We next construct an honest observed-data interval with vanishing worst-case expected length.  Work under the conditional design law given \(E^c\).  Since \(E\) is determined before block \(2\), it belongs to every \(H_{2i}\).  Define the observable variables
\[
 X_i=2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_1\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i}
     -2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_0\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i},
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
On \(E^c\), both available arms have conditional probability \(1/2\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) and the observation map therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i\mid H_{2i},E^c]
 =Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)
\]
and, by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcomes}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i^2\mid H_{2i},E^c]
 =2Y_{2i}(z_1)^2+2Y_{2i}(z_0)^2
 \le4M^2.
\]
Because \(q_2=1\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) identifies the average of the first display with \(\tau_W\).  Hence
\[
 \Delta_i=X_i-\{Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)\}
\]
is a martingale difference under the conditional law given \(E^c\).  If \(i<j\), then \(\Delta_i\) is \(H_{2j}\)-measurable, so iterated conditioning gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i\Delta_j\mid E^c]
 =\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 \left[
  \Delta_i\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_j\mid H_{2j},E^c]
  \,\middle|\,E^c
 \right]=0.
\]
The increments are orthogonal.  Conditional variance is bounded by conditional second moment, so, uniformly over \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
 [ (\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W)^2\mid E^c]
 &=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}
   \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i^2\mid E^c]\\
 &\le\frac{4M^2}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Set
\[
 \beta=\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}
       =\frac{\alpha/2}{1-\alpha/2}>0,
 \qquad
 t_n=\frac{2M}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(t_n<2M\).  Define a deterministic, schedule-independent observed-data kernel that reports the singleton \(\{0\}\) on \(E\), and on \(E^c\) reports
\[
 J_n=
 [\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-t_n,
   \Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)+t_n]
 \cap[-2M,2M].
\]
This is always a nonempty closed interval because its projected center belongs to \([-2M,2M]\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) give \(\tau_W\in[-2M,2M]\).  The metric projection inequality used in Definition \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\) therefore gives
\[
 |\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-\tau_W|
 \le|\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W|.
\]
For \(t_n>0\), the pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{|x|>t_n\}\le x^2/t_n^2\) and the preceding second-moment bound imply
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\notin J_n\mid E^c)
 \le\frac{4M^2/n}{t_n^2}=\beta.
\]
We make no coverage claim on \(E\).  Nevertheless, because \(P^O_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(E)=\varepsilon\) for every schedule,
\[
 P^K_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\in I_K)
 \ge(1-\varepsilon)(1-\beta)=1-\alpha.
\]
Thus the kernel belongs to \(\mathcal C_\alpha\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\).  Its singleton branch has length zero and \(\operatorname{len}(J_n)\le2t_n\), whence, uniformly over the schedule class,
\[
 \mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star
 \le(1-\varepsilon)2t_n
 =\frac{4M(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
Combining this inequality with \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) yields
\[
 \frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
      {\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}
 \le\frac{2(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every member of the sequence satisfies all primitive assumptions with \(p_{\min,n}=\varepsilon/n>0\).  If a positive comparison constant depending only on \(\alpha\) existed, applying it to this sequence and taking the displayed limit would be a contradiction.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), let \(Y^{(0)}\in\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\) be the all-zero fixed schedule.  For any set \(S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}\), define its target weight and masked event by
\[
 w(S)=\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b},
 \qquad
 E_S=\{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}.
\]
If
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}(E_S)\ge1-\eta_\alpha,
\]
then
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]
The probability in the premise is computable as a finite sum of products of the known sequential propensities evaluated on zero-outcome histories that avoid the focal arm at every position in \(S\); propensities may otherwise depend arbitrarily on the observed past.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\).  Define two fixed schedules \(Y^-\) and \(Y^+\) by
\[
 Y^-_{bi}(z_1)=-M,
 \qquad
 Y^+_{bi}(z_1)=M
 \quad\text{for }(b,i)\in S,
\]
and set every other available potential outcome, including focal outcomes outside \(S\), equal to zero under both schedules.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) holds because all coordinates belong to \([-M,M]\).  Every control potential outcome is zero, so every control block mean is zero and
\[
 \sum_{b=1}^{B-1}|\mu_{b+1}-\mu_b|=0\le\gamma.
\]
Thus Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:control\text{-}tv}\) holds at budget \(\gamma\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def:schedule\text{-}family}\) gives
\[
 Y^-,Y^+\in\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:availability\text{-}window}\) ensures that \(z_1\) is available at every position of \(S\).  Since the target weights are positive, Definition \(\mathrm{def:target}\) gives
\[
 \tau_W(Y^-)=-M w(S),
 \qquad
 \tau_W(Y^+)=M w(S).
\]

We next compare the two observed-data laws.  On any assignment prefix that has not assigned \(z_1\) at a position in \(S\), every outcome observed so far under \(Y^-\), \(Y^+\), and \(Y^{(0)}\) equals zero.  Start with the empty history and proceed through the finite lexicographic order on \(\mathcal T\).  Whenever the three prefixes coincide and remain compatible with \(E_S\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization}\) evaluates the same known function \(p_{bi}(\cdot\mid H_{bi})\) at the same assignment--outcome history; hence the conditional probability of every next arm is identical under all three schedules.  Induction over the enrollment positions yields
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-}(E_S)
 =P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}(E_S)
 =P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}(E_S)=:q_S.
\]
The same induction proves equality of the restrictions of \(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-}\) and \(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}\) to \(E_S\), because both assignments and recorded outcomes coincide along every record in that event.

On \(E_S^c\), let \((b,i)\) be the first position in \(S\) assigned to \(z_1\).  The full record then contains the observed value \(-M\) under \(Y^-\) and \(M\) under \(Y^+\) at that same assigned position.  Since \(M>0\), no full record in the restriction of the first law to \(E_S^c\) belongs to the support of the restriction of the second law to \(E_S^c\).  The two laws therefore have a common subprobability restriction of mass \(q_S\) on \(E_S\) and mutually singular complementary restrictions.  By the definition of total variation on the finite record space,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}
 \left(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^-},P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^+}\right)
 =1-q_S
 \le\eta_\alpha.
\]

In Definition \(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}information\text{-}modulus}\), take \(\Pi_0=\delta_{Y^-}\) and \(\Pi_1=\delta_{Y^+}\).  The preceding membership calculation proves that both priors are supported on \(\mathcal Y_{M,\gamma}\); the preceding total-variation calculation verifies the information constraint; and
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\operatorname{supp}(\Pi_0)}\tau_W(Y)+2M w(S)
 =-M w(S)+2M w(S)
 =M w(S)
 =\inf_{Y\in\operatorname{supp}(\Pi_1)}\tau_W(Y).
\]
Thus \(\Delta=2M w(S)\) is feasible in the defining supremum, and
\[
 \Omega_{\mathcal D,\gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\ge2M w(S).
\]

For computability, let \(\mathcal A_S\) be the finite set of complete assignment paths with no \(z_1\) assignment at a position in \(S\).  Along the all-zero schedule, a path \(z=(z_{bi})\) has probability
\[
 \prod_{(b,i)\in\mathcal T}
 p_{bi}(z_{bi}\mid h^0_{bi}(z)),
\]
where \(h^0_{bi}(z)\) is the prefix consisting of the earlier assignments in \(z\) and their zero observed outcomes.  Hence
\[
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}(E_S)
 =\sum_{z\in\mathcal A_S}
 \prod_{(b,i)\in\mathcal T}
 p_{bi}(z_{bi}\mid h^0_{bi}(z)).
\]
The set \(\mathcal T\) and every availability set are finite, and the propensities are known, so this is a finite, explicitly evaluable sum.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the primitive sequential-randomization, availability, positivity, boundedness, and control-total-variation conditions, every admissible experiment satisfies
\[
 \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Let \(Y^{(0)}\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}\) be the all-zero fixed schedule. The same experiment also has the computable masked-history lower certificate
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge \eta_\alpha
 \max_{\substack{S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}:\\ P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}\{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}\ge1-\eta_\alpha}}
 \left\{2M\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b}\right\}.
\]
The feasible collection is nonempty and the maximum is computable by finite enumeration. No constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can strengthen the first lower bound to \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over the primitive adaptive-design class. Indeed, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and \(M>0\), there is a sequence of admissible experiments with \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(\Gamma=0\), and a positive propensity floor in every experiment such that \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\). Coverage and expected length use the same extended design law, and the minimax infimum ranges over every schedule-independent auxiliary-randomized, variable-length observed-data interval kernel.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original alpha-only equivalence is false on the unchanged primitive adaptive-design class. A rare-history sequence has clipped AIPW radius exactly \(2M\) while the minimax expected length tends to zero. The narrowed theorem retains the universal mixture-modulus lower bound and factor-two constructive upper bound, adds the sound computable masked-history lower certificate, and states the generic impossibility explicitly without assuming a radius-to-modulus comparison.

proposed.statement:
Under the primitive sequential-randomization, availability, positivity, boundedness, and control-total-variation conditions, every admissible experiment satisfies
\[
 \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)
 \le \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Let \(Y^{(0)}\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}\) be the all-zero fixed schedule.  The same experiment also has the computable masked-history lower certificate
\[
 \mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
 \ge
 \eta_\alpha
 \max_{\substack{
 S\subseteq\{(b,i)\in\mathcal T:b\in W\}:\\
 P^O_{\mathcal D,Y^{(0)}}
 \{Z_{bi}\ne z_1\text{ for every }(b,i)\in S\}
 \ge1-\eta_\alpha}}
 \left\{2M\sum_{(b,i)\in S}\frac{q_b}{n_b}\right\}.
\]
The feasible collection in this maximum is nonempty because it contains \(S=\varnothing\), and the maximum is obtained by finite enumeration of subsets and zero-outcome assignment paths.  No constant \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) can strengthen the first lower bound to \(c_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) uniformly over the primitive adaptive-design class.  Indeed, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and \(M>0\), there is a sequence of admissible experiments with \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(\Gamma=0\), and a positive propensity floor in every experiment such that \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) and \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star/\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\to0\).  Coverage and expected length use the same extended design law, and the minimax infimum ranges over every schedule-independent auxiliary-randomized, variable-length observed-data interval kernel.
proposed.justification: The repaired theorem identifies the two universally valid scales, supplies a directly computable all-kernel lower certificate, and proves that the optimized predictable-AIPW radius is not uniformly minimax-equivalent over arbitrary adaptive histories.
proposed.gap: Gaussian and model-based platform results do not capture the rare-history expected-length obstruction. The primitive-class radius equivalence is false; the valid lower objects are the observed-law mixture modulus and computable testing certificates such as the masked-focal construction.
proposed.consumer: Trial software may always report the projected uniformly honest interval and its factor-two upper guarantee. It must not label the optimized radius minimax-equivalent without additional independently justified design structure; it can compute the masked-history expression as a certified lower benchmark.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim uses two newly proved load-bearing certificates and removes the false alpha-only lower comparison, so the theorem's dependencies, free symbols, and result notes must be synchronized with its post-image.

prose_updates.tldr: A cumulative-discrepancy linear program gives the exact worst-case bias from borrowing nonconcurrent controls, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope. Projection yields an everywhere-nonempty, uniformly design-honest interval whose worst-case expected length is at most twice the clipped optimized radius. For every adaptive design, every honest observed-data interval kernel also obeys the generic lower bound \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\). A masked-focal construction supplies an additional finite-tree computable lower certificate by locating target-weighted positions that the all-zero adaptive tree fails to assign to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\). An explicit three-block rare-history sequence proves that no positive constant depending only on \(\alpha\) can lower-compare minimax expected length to the optimized AIPW radius over the unrestricted primitive class: the radius remains \(2M\) while an honest variable-length interval has expected length tending to zero. Thus the radius is a constructive upper scale, not a generic minimax characterization. The separate KKT certificate still determines strict improvement over the concurrent AIPW rule. At zero drift the convex program is purely information-optimal, while at vacuous drift the full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel values agree under the accepted structural invariance of propensities to off-window outcomes. The enumerated one-unit three-block experiment retains its certified zero-drift minimax value \(0.7M\); no positive-drift value is inferred from it.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers study parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work gives minimax expected-length theory in nonadaptive observation experiments. None supplies a fixed-schedule adaptive-randomization theorem that separates a universally honest predictable-AIPW upper radius from the smaller expected length attainable by variable-length intervals when severe propensities occur only on rare histories. The unrestricted alpha-only equivalence is therefore not merely absent from the literature; it is false.
project_justification.niche: The note treats the adaptive assignment tree as part of the experiment and keeps fixed potential outcomes distinct from assignment randomness. It combines the exact support function of the bounded-total-variation control-mean class with actual-history martingale information, an all-kernel observed-law mixture modulus, and an explicit finite-tree masked-focal testing certificate. This separates the causal finite-population contrast, an implementable honest AIPW radius, and the minimax expected length over all observed-data interval kernels.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a sharp drift-bias dual, a convex-program projected interval with worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, a generic mixture-modulus lower bound for every schedule-independent randomized interval, a computable masked-history lower certificate, and an explicit rare-history impossibility for any unrestricted alpha-only radius comparison. The optimizer certificate characterizes strict gain over the concurrent AIPW rule rather than over the all-kernel minimax value. The accepted boundary results remain intact: zero drift removes the borrowing bias, and vacuous drift gives equality with the concurrent-only all-kernel benchmark only when propensity updates are structurally unchanged by off-window potential-outcome changes holding assignments and window outcomes fixed.

prose_updates.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze all-control versus concurrent-only platform procedures under specified linear, step, fixed-effect, mixed-effect, or spline time models and emphasize bias, type-I error, and power. MarschnerSchou2024 defines concurrency through randomized cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies a superpopulation efficiency problem for the concurrent estimand. Those results motivate the platform setting but do not give uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a total-variation drift class or minimax expected length over schedule-independent observed-data kernels. LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template; here the information envelope averages under each schedule's actual adaptive assignment law, so a rare branch contributes through both its probability and its inverse propensity. ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 provide Gaussian bias--variance and mixture-modulus analogies, but their likelihood geometry does not justify a radius comparison after observed outcomes feed back into later assignments. The rare-history construction proves that an alpha-only comparison is false for the primitive adaptive class. The positive all-kernel statements are instead the generic observed-law modulus bound and the masked-focal certificate: two explicit bounded schedules coincide on a sufficiently probable zero-outcome subtree and have a computable target separation. No comparison of either lower object to the optimized AIPW radius is claimed. SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 selects external-control weights under an estimated bias cap, but its estimand, confounding model, bootstrap interval, and guarantee differ from the present fixed-population randomization result. AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 provide bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, TV borrowing, or adaptive-history masking.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale but is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale. The counterexample exploits the distinction between a second-moment interval that pays for a rare low-propensity branch and a variable-length procedure that can spend part of its allowed miscoverage on that branch. Its sequence has a positive propensity floor in every experiment, but the floor decreases with the block-two sample size; whether additional independently motivated uniform reachability or fixed-floor restrictions yield a sharper radius comparison is not settled here. The masked-history expression is an exact, finite-tree computable lower certificate and lower-bounds the observed-law modulus construction by explicit testing schedules, but no comparison of it or the modulus to the optimized AIPW radius is asserted. The vacuous-drift reduction separately requires propensity invariance across schedules when only off-window outcomes change; mere predictability does not imply that invariance.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the experiment's only source of randomness. The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest for every design satisfying the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions, with no regression-consistency or asymptotic-normality premise. The all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound and the finite masked-focal testing certificate are also generic. No universal alpha-only equivalence between minimax expected length and the optimized AIPW radius is claimed: an explicit admissible three-block sequence refutes it while maintaining positivity in every experiment. The masked-focal result supplies a computable lower benchmark only; it is not used as a witness-form premise for any radius comparison. The KKT result compares NCC and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values. At zero drift, equal control block means eliminate borrowing bias and leave the program to minimize assignment-law-averaged information; under the boundary proposition's nondegeneracy condition every block receives positive weight. At vacuous drift, full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel minimax values coincide only under the accepted structural condition that propensity updates are invariant to off-window potential-outcome changes with assignments and window outcomes fixed. The separate finite three-block LP asserts only its proved zero-drift value \(0.7M\), supported by matching primal and dual certificates. No claim is made that the drift budget is identified from trial data, that the masked certificate is necessary, or that the finite LP has the same value at positive drift.

statement_notes.justification: The repaired headline gives the strongest conclusion supported on the primitive adaptive class: a universal observed-law-modulus lower bound, a factor-two constructive upper bound, a computable masked-history lower certificate, and a theorem-level impossibility of any alpha-only lower comparison with the optimized AIPW radius.
statement_notes.gap: Existing platform and Gaussian minimax results do not capture the rare-history expected-length obstruction. The formerly claimed primitive-class equivalence is false; a sharper radius comparison would require independently motivated structure beyond the frozen assumptions and is not claimed here.
statement_notes.consumer: The NCC implementation can always report the projected uniformly honest interval and its upper guarantee, and can compute the masked-history lower benchmark. It must present the optimized radius as an implementable conservative scale rather than as the unrestricted minimax expected length.
